label: The analytic shortcut must stay under simulation's supervision
rationale: Closing section gives three advantages of computational methods (explainable, robust, debuggable), two drawbacks (slow, nondeterministic), and a three-step process ending in mutual validation between computational and analytic results.

label: The Central Limit Theorem has three conditions, and two of them fail on ordinary engineering data
rationale: CLT stated with identical-distribution, independence, and finite-mean-and-variance conditions, then deliberately broken: Pareto alpha=1 is nothing like normal at n=100, and serially correlated exponentials with rho=0.8 converge slowly or not at all.

label: Every named test is shown to be an approximation before it is used
rationale: The t test, the correlation t transform, and chi-squared are each validated by plotting the simulated null distribution against the analytic model; analytic p-values are then checked against ttest_ind, pearsonr, and chisquare.

label: The standard-error formula is derived, not asserted
rationale: A Normal class with distribution algebra (add, sum, scalar multiply/divide, subtract) yields sd/sqrt(n) as the net effect of multiplying variance by n then dividing by n squared; each algebraic step is checked against a random sample first.

label: The normal probability plot is a parameter-free fit diagnostic
rationale: Introduced explicitly because overlaying a fitted CDF depends on how well you estimated the parameters; used to diagnose the Adelie penguin weights as a mixture of two normals.

label: A relationship can be statistically significant and useless for prediction
rationale: Maternal age vs birth weight has a small p-value and a small R-squared; the book names this as a common source of confusion and resolves it.

label: Expected remaining lifetime stops decreasing
rationale: Expected time to delivery falls from 3.2 weeks at week 36 to about 0.6 weeks at week 39, then levels off at weeks 40-43 rather than continuing to fall.

label: Confidence intervals cover only sampling variability
rationale: Sampling bias, self-selection, and measurement error are separate sources of error and often larger; the telephone-sampling example makes this concrete.

label: Time series decomposition through ARIMA on real electricity data
rationale: Late chapter builds seasonal decomposition, multiplicative models, autoregression, moving average, and ARIMA prediction on EIA renewable-generation data.
